A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same internal-supervision and curriculum-based self-improvement study, despite the revised title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Janus-Pro experiments on generation, understanding, curriculum learning, learning dynamics, and corrupted-label co-degradation.

after.justification: v2 reports original multi-model gap measurements, Janus-Pro and Show-o fine-tuning experiments, human evaluations, understanding benchmarks, and ablations.

M1.justification: The operative framework remains internal image scoring, generation-side SFT or DPO with auxiliary NLL, and curriculum replay of previously unusable prompts. v2's algorithms and probability-based selection details expand documentation without establishing a different underlying method. CLO-SFT/CLO-DPO become C-SFT/C-DPO.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's compositional-image tasks, v2 adds GenEval, Science-T2I-S physics/chemistry/biology tasks, and POPE, MMB, SEED, GQA, and MMMU understanding evaluations. It also reports non-spatial relations and broadens training from spatial prompts to multiple compositional subtasks.

E2.justification: v1 Table 3 primarily compares Janus-Pro variants with T2I-R1. v2 retains T2I-R1, adds Hermesflow for Show-o, and reports eight generation-only comparators in Table 1, including SDv1.5, SD-XL-base-1.0, and FLUX.1. Appendix F.3 additionally compares self-improvement against Qwen-assisted SFT.

E3.justification: v1 documents 700 spatial training samples and 120 training epochs; v2 describes about 6000 candidate prompts and 20 SFT or 30 DPO epochs. Curriculum replay moves from epoch 60 to epoch 10. v2 adds Show-o training settings, difficulty-stratified evaluation, human checking, and exact-match understanding evaluations; v1's spatial-training ID/OOD design is no longer retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds human-versus-Qwen checks, similarity controls supporting the eNTK explanation, single-branch versus joint curriculum-data expansion, and component, replay-timing, and external-reward ablations. Conversely, v1's corrupted-supervision co-degradation experiments and Top-K generation-proxy sensitivity plots are removed, rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Statistical displays change: v1 Figure 8 presents sample-level dynamics with boxplots, while v2 adds error-bar summaries for similarity analyses in Figures 7, 13, 15, and 16. The new bars are not defined. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or benchmark confidence intervals, so additional experimental replication is not established.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark, human-check, and ablation results are added, while co-degradation results are removed. Janus-Pro SFT's reported texture generation score changes from 44.90 in v1 Table 3 to 53.93 in v2 Table 5; these belong to different training settings and are not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v1's single-token dynamics and linear-network case study are substantially revised into multi-token SFT analysis with explicit causal-masking and shared-tokenizer assumptions. v2 adds a DPO proposition and corresponding proofs in Appendices D–E, addressing extensions explicitly left for future work in v1. It also introduces a threshold rule connecting likelihoods to binary understanding decisions.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds both co-improvement and co-degradation, including the inability of intrinsic metrics to distinguish them. v2 drops the co-degradation contribution and foregrounds systematic multi-model gap verification and stronger comparisons against externally rewarded systems. The central internal-supervision, co-improvement, and curriculum claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 removes the specific warning that unification can improve while both capabilities deteriorate. It adds substantive discussion of task-difficulty confounding, relative gaps versus absolute ability, Qwen's limitations on difficult tasks, and why larger-gap tasks supply more training data. Its mechanism discussion emphasizes shared eNTK dominance, while acknowledging that the origin of this sharing remains unresolved.

D1.justification: v2 adds a detailed hyperparameter table, the full scoring prompt, probability-based image selection details, image sizes, candidate counts, optimizer parameters, batch sizes, loss weights, implementation repositories, and VLMEvalKit usage. Appendix D documents similarity computation. v1's explicit checkpoint-selection rule is no longer stated, but implementation documentation is substantially expanded overall.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reorganized around gap measurement, mitigation, and co-improvement, with stronger positioning against external-assessment and external-supervision approaches. v2 adds works such as Yan et al. on joint understanding/generation benefits and Xie et al. on reconstruction alignment, alongside broader architecture and benchmark literature. References supporting v1's self-correction failure discussion are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, terminology, and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Related work moves near the beginning; phenomenon verification, method evaluation, mechanism analysis, and curriculum learning receive separate sections. The takeaway-box structure is replaced, and the appendices are reorganized into six thematic sections with a contents page.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the visual presentation: the opening example is simplified, multi-model difficulty plots and algorithm blocks are added, and comparison tables gain model groups and supervision indicators. Expanded appendix tables, similarity plots, and qualitative examples replace or supplement earlier displays. v1's corruption figures, curriculum rings, and pipeline diagram are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical support through multiple architectures, independent understanding benchmarks, human checking, and targeted ablations. Expanded multi-token/DPO derivations and implementation details also make the central argument more assessable. Removing the co-degradation experiments and intrinsic-metric warning weakens coverage of failure conditions, but the stronger validation of the central self-improvement claims provides a substantial net quality gain.
